Q: Pause shell script until user presses enter A:

Inside of bash you can use read -p, however this is not POSIX compliant.

TL;DR

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." && read <"/dev/tty"

Full explanation & options

For POSIX compliance, you can use a couple different options:

Simplest option, and best one for general uses

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." && read

A bit more tight on what you can input, and fixes line ending.

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." && read -rsn 1 <"/dev/tty" && printf '\n'

VERY tight, and handles input by processing the byte size of the user's input.

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." >"/dev/stdout"
_t="$(stty -g)"
stty -echo -icanon min 1 time 0
dd bs=1 count=1 1>"/dev/null" 2>&1
stty "$_t"
printf '\n' >"/dev/stdout"

Single line

printf '%s' "Press any key to continue..." >"/dev/stdout"; _t="$(stty -g)"; stty -echo -icanon min 1 time 0; dd bs=1 count=1 1>"/dev/null" 2>&1; stty "$_t"; printf '\n' >"/dev/stdout"

The only 'needed' snippet is:

read

This already handles input the way we want, so it can just be used alone.

-p arg

The -p arg according to the read --help command on bash 5.3.9(1)-release states:

-p PROMPT
Output the string PROMPT without a trailing newline before

All of these have been tested using bash and sh. Specifically (Shebangs):

#!/usr/bin/bash

And

#!/usr/bin/sh

Also tested using shellcheck:

shellcheck --severity=style --shell=sh --list-optional --color=always ./test.sh | bat

Resources

Host Page

linux.org stty man page (POSIX)
linux.org dd main page (POSIX)
opengroup.org POSIX standard
github.com sh formatted and syntax checker

Q: Google Drive Folder File Counting Script A:

While a link to a spreadsheet might be helpful, it's better to include all the relevant details directly in the question body. As you have shared your spreadsheet to allow anyoone with the link to edit, this is even more relevant as the spreadsheet and the bound script might be changed at any time.

On the other hand, you have told us about what you need and what you want but you haven't made a question. In regards the issue, you haven't mentioned what you have done to understand it. If you haven't done anything, I suggest you to start by looking to the execution logs. Look if there are an error and if there are custom messages about the execution progress that could help you to understand why the issue occurs.

Q: Flutter Web Firebase (No Firebase App '[DEFAULT]' has been created) A:

@Thom A
I guess you duplicated settings.
In my view, you don't need to add Firebase config in main.dart.
Is it for your android/ios/windows build? If not, you can remove it.
Plus, in index.html, you can add firebase config json in web project(not the same config as android or ios project).

Q: Where to place window.addEventListener('online' A:

In the root +layout.svelte, via <svelte:window>

<svelte:window ononline={onOnline} onoffline={onOffline} />

You can also bind the online status to a state variable.

<svelte:window bind:online={online} />

(Also, please don't use "best practices" questions, they break everything that is good about StackOverflow.)
